stages.alerts_dayplan:
## ⚠️ CRITICAL ALERTS

🔴 **Drain output changed: serosanguinous → cloudy/greenish-brown, volume 45mL → 120mL overnight** — This is the most concerning finding. POD5 from ileocolic anastomosis with changed drain character and volume reversal is an anastomotic leak until proven otherwise. Need urgent CT with oral and rectal contrast.

🔴 **WBC 19.4, ↑ from 13.1 yesterday** — Significant spike. Combined with fever, tachycardia, hypotension, and drain changes, this is an evolving sepsis picture from an intra-abdominal source.

🔴 **Lactate 3.8 (first draw since admission)** — Elevated with hemodynamic instability. Need serial trending q4-6h to assess resuscitation response and guide decision-making.

🟡 **Cr 2.3, ↑ from 1.8 (baseline 1.4–1.6)** — Worsening AKI. UOP declining: 37.5 → 28 → 20 mL/hr over 72h. Likely prerenal from sepsis/hypovolemia. If CT with contrast needed, the clinical benefit outweighs contrast risk here — bolus first.

🟡 **Hgb 8.9, ↓ from 10.4 on POD1** — Steady downtrend. Type and screen should be active from pre-op. Transfuse if <7 or if heading to OR. Consider lower threshold given active sepsis.

🟡 **SpO2 88% → 94% on 2L NC** — New O2 requirement. COPD with poor IS compliance (400-600mL, goal 1500). Differential: post-op atelectasis, aspiration, early pneumonia, or sepsis-related. Need CXR.

🟡 **Blood glucose 186 → 244, escalating SSI (2u → 6u)** — Poorly controlled. Worsening hyperglycemia can be an early sign of sepsis and impairs anastomotic healing and immune function. Target <180 per NICE-SUGAR.

🟡 **Metoprolol held — HR 118** — Appropriate given BP 98/60. Tachycardia is sepsis-driven. Treat the source, not the rate.

🟡 **Enoxaparin last dose >24h ago** — Due 03/02 0900. Hold if OR likely today. But high DVT risk: cancer + immobility + POD5. Reassess after surgical decision is made.

🟡 **Tiotropium not restarted** — Home COPD inhaler not on inpatient med list. Should have been continued post-op. Add to orders once acute issue addressed.

🟢 **Pathology: pT3N1b adenocarcinoma, 3/12 nodes, LVI present** — Will need adjuvant FOLFOX per NCCN. Not urgent today, but flag for oncology referral at discharge. CEA baseline 14.2 for surveillance. KRAS and MSI still pending.

## 📋 DAY PLAN

**Discharge blocker:** Suspected anastomotic leak with developing sepsis. Goal today is diagnosis and source control.

**CRITICAL — NEXT 2 HOURS:**
- [ ] Call attending with overnight changes: drain character, WBC spike, lactate, hemodynamics
- [ ] CT abdomen/pelvis with oral and rectal contrast — STAT
- [ ] IVF bolus 30mL/kg crystalloid — monitor UOP closely given CKD
- [ ] Blood cultures x2 before next pip-tazo dose
- [ ] Repeat lactate in 4 hours
- [ ] Type and screen confirmation, CBC, BMP

**IF LEAK CONFIRMED ON CT:**
- [ ] Consent for exploratory laparotomy ± washout ± diverting ileostomy ± anastomotic revision
- [ ] Notify anesthesia — ASA III, COPD, CKD, active sepsis
- [ ] Hold enoxaparin (last dose >24h ago — cleared for OR)
- [ ] Strict NPO (already not tolerating PO)
- [ ] Update wife Margaret and daughter Sarah (healthcare POA)

**ONGOING:**
- [ ] CXR for new O2 requirement
- [ ] Aggressive IS, albuterol nebs, consider CPAP — pulmonary toilet is critical with his COPD
- [ ] Restart tiotropium inhaler (home med, missed)
- [ ] Tighten glucose: increase SSI coverage or start low-dose insulin drip if heading to OR, target <180
- [ ] Continue pip-tazo — appropriate empiric for intra-abdominal sepsis
- [ ] Strict I&O via foley
- [ ] Hold PT until acute issue resolved

**NON-URGENT (flag for later):**
- [ ] Oncology referral for adjuvant chemotherapy discussion (pT3N1b)
- [ ] CEA 14.2 baseline documented for post-treatment surveillance
- [ ] Follow up KRAS and MSI from pathology
stages.presentation: James Carter is a 71-year-old male, hospital day 10, POD5 from an open right hemicolectomy for an obstructing hepatic flexure mass — path came back yesterday showing a moderately differentiated adenocarcinoma, pT3N1b, 3 of 12 nodes positive with LVI. Overnight he deteriorated significantly. His drain output changed from 45mL of serosanguinous to 120mL of cloudy greenish-brown fluid. His white count spiked from 13.1 to 19.4, we drew a lactate for the first time since admission which came back at 3.8, and his creatinine is worsening at 2.3 from a baseline of 1.4 to 1.6. He's febrile to 38.2, tachycardic at 118 with his metoprolol held for a pressure of 98/60, and he desatted to 88% overnight — now on 2L. His urine output has been declining too, down to 20mL an hour. His sugars have also been harder to control, up to 244 on escalating sliding scale. He does have underlying COPD and his incentive spirometry has been poor. [PENDING — abdominal exam is critical this morning]. My concern is anastomotic leak. I think we need an urgent CT with oral and rectal contrast, and I'd like to have a low threshold for taking him back if it confirms a leak.

## CARTER, James | 71M | 8W-816A | HD10, POD#5
s/p open right hemicolectomy for obstructing hepatic flexure adenocarcinoma (pT3N1b)

### Overnight
- Drain output CHANGED: 45mL serosanguinous → 120mL cloudy/greenish-brown
- WBC 13.1 → 19.4, new lactate 3.8, Cr 1.8 → 2.3 (baseline 1.4-1.6)
- Febrile 38.2°C, HR 118, BP 98/60 — metoprolol held
- SpO2 dropped to 88% → placed on 2L NC (now 94%)
- UOP declining: 37.5 → 28 → 20 mL/hr over 72h
- Pip-tazo started 0600 by overnight resident after drain output change
- Hgb continuing downtrend: 10.4 → 9.4 → 8.9
- BS 244 at 0100, required 6u SSI (was 2u three days ago)
- Not eating, not ambulating, did not get OOB overnight

### Current Status
Septic picture developing. The drain output is the key finding — cloudy/bilious fluid from a right paracolic gutter drain on POD5 from an ileocolic anastomosis is a leak until proven otherwise. Hemodynamically borderline, AKI worsening, new O2 requirement, deconditioning. COPD with IS only 400-600mL (goal 1500).

### Yesterday's Plan → Today
- **Continue diet as tolerated** → Not eating. Nauseous. Zero PO overnight. Formalize NPO.
- **Encourage ambulation, goal 4x with PT** → Did not ambulate POD4-5. Refused PT. Deconditioning.
- **Monitor WBC — if rising, consider CT** → WBC jumped 13.1 → 19.4. CT is needed NOW.
- **Drain to remain, monitor character** → Character changed: serosanguinous → cloudy/greenish-brown. Volume tripled. This is the finding.
- **DVT prophylaxis with enoxaparin** → Last dose 03/01 0900. Hold if OR likely. High risk: cancer + immobility + POD5.
- **Sliding scale insulin** → Sugars worsening: 186 → 244. Escalating requirements. Needs tighter control.
- **Repeat labs AM** → Done. Everything is worse.
- **Path results — discuss with patient/family** → pT3N1b, 3/12 nodes. Discussion deferred for acute deterioration. Oncology referral when stable.

### Key Context
CKD3 baseline Cr 1.4-1.6, now 2.3 — limits contrast but CT is necessary here. COPD 40 pack-year — poor IS compliance, new O2 requirement, tiotropium not restarted (missed home med). Diabetes A1c 8.4 — sugars poorly controlled on SSI, hyperglycemia impairs healing. Lisinopril allergy (cough), no antibiotic allergies. 19Fr Blake drain in right paracolic gutter — the critical monitoring tool right now. Wife Margaret and daughter Sarah (healthcare POA, 555-0142) — need update today regardless of CT result. Full code.
